Above all, **he was an inventor, creating solutions to common problems, innovating new technology, and even making life a little more musical.**
 
• **James Clerk Maxwel**l is most famous for his **theory of electromagnetism,** which showed that **light was electromagnetic radiation**. His theory is considered to have paved the way for both quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory of special relativity.
 
• **Andre-Marie Ampere** **the astatic needle**, a critical component of the modern astatic galvanometer, and was the first to demonstrate that a magnetic field is generated when two parallel wires are charged with electricity. He is generally credited as one of the first to discover **electromagnetism**.

questions.question: The lifting of an object up and down, the parade of an army and the free fall of a heavy object are all examples of which motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rectilinear motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rectilinear motion **is also known as **Linear motion**.
 
• **Rectilinear motion **is **one-dimensional **motion along **a straight line**, and can therefore be described mathematically using **only one spatial dimension**.
 
• A **linear motion **in which the **direction **of the **velocity remains constant **and the **path is a straight line**.
 
• **Gravitational forces **acting on **objects resulting **in **free fall **is an **example **of rectilinear motion.
 
• **Kids sliding down from a slide is **a rectilinear motion.
 
• The motion of **planes in the sky **is a rectilinear motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic motion **is a motion **repeated in equal intervals of time**.
 
• Periodic motion is performed, for example, **by a rocking chair**, a **bouncing ball**, a **vibrating tuning fork**, a **swing in motion**, the **Earth **in its **orbit around the Sun**, and **a water wave**.
 
• **Rotational motion **can be defined as the **motion of an object **around a **circular path**, in a **fixed orbit**.
 
• A **motion repeating itself **is referred to as **periodic or oscillatory motion**.
 
• An **object in **such motion **oscillates **about an **equilibrium position **due to a **restoring force **or **torque**.

questions.question: According to the Henry Cavendish experiment conducted in 1797-1798, what was the value of the universal constant of gravity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__6.75 × 10-11 N m2/kg2__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__The **Cavendish experiment **was performed in **1797–1798 **by **English scientist Henry Cavendish**.
 
• It was the **first experiment **to **measure **the **force of gravity **between **masses **in the **laboratory **and the **first to yield accurate values **for the **gravitational constant**.
 
• The **Cavendish experiment **was **significant **not only for **measuring Earth's density **(and thus its mass) but also for **proving that Newton's law of gravitation **worked on **scales much **smaller than those of **the solar system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry Cavendish FRS **was an **English natural philosopher **and **scientist **who was an **important experimental and theoretical chemist **and **physicist**. He is noted for **his discovery of hydrogen**, which he termed **"inflammable air".**
 
• He was **born **on **10 October 1731**, **in Nice in France**.
 
• He died on **24 February 1810**, in **London**, **United Kingdom**
